text:
### 8.1 Maintaining Independence  
**Safeguards:**
- No operational responsibilities
- No decision-making authority
- No conflict of interest roles
- Separate reporting to Board Audit Committee
- Budget approved by Board (not management)
- Staff appraisals reviewed by Board chair  
**Prohibited Activities:**
- Internal Audit staff cannot audit departments where recently managed
- Internal Audit staff cannot audit their own work
- Internal Audit staff cannot approve transactions or controls they audit
- Internal Audit cannot advise on strategy (can audit strategic decisions)

The department's budget is approved by the Board rather than management, and staff appraisals are reviewed by the Board chair.

raw_entities.name: Board Audit Committee Oversight of Internal Audit Independence
raw_entities.description: The Board Audit Committee exercises governance oversight of Internal Audit independence through separate reporting lines, budget approval authority, and staff appraisal review. This governance structure ensures Internal Audit maintains operational and decision-making independence from management.
context: Separate reporting to Board Audit Committee
Budget approved by Board (not management)
Staff appraisals reviewed by Board chair

raw_entities.name: Internal Audit Independence and Conflict of Interest Controls
raw_entities.description: Internal Audit has established comprehensive safeguards to maintain independence, including prohibitions on auditing recently managed departments, auditing own work, approving transactions or controls under audit, and providing strategic advice. These controls ensure audit objectivity and prevent conflicts of interest.
context: No conflict of interest roles
Internal Audit staff cannot audit departments where recently managed
Internal Audit staff cannot audit their own work
Internal Audit staff cannot approve transactions or controls they audit

raw_entities.name: Internal Audit Scope Limitation on Strategic Advisory
raw_entities.description: Internal Audit is prohibited from advising on strategy to maintain independence, though the function retains the ability to audit strategic decisions made by management. This boundary preserves audit objectivity while allowing evaluation of strategic decision-making processes.
context: Internal Audit cannot advise on strategy (can audit strategic decisions)
